I have been farming these fields in Quzhou for 50 years. I am 73 now, but I still know every mu of my 16.9 mu plot. My household has six people, and some of the younger ones work off-farm in the county town, so I manage most of the farm work myself, though they come back to help during harvest and sowing. I have a well, so water is reliable, which is a blessing on the North China Plain.

This year, I will stick to my wheat-maize double cropping system. It is what this soil knows, and it is what I know. In autumn, I will prepare the whole 16.9 mu for winter wheat. I will use rotary tillage to break up the stubble and level the field — I am too old for deep ploughing, and rotary tillage has worked well for years. I will sow an improved wheat variety, probably something like Luyuan 502 or Jimai 22, seeds I trust from the local supply shop. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea later, totaling about 18 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. Wheat needs water at critical times, so I will irrigate four times: once before winter to ensure safe overwintering, once at green-up in spring, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. I will spray pesticides three times — herbicide after sowing, then insecticide and fungicide in spring when the weather warms up. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather cooperates.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize on the same 16.9 mu. There is never much time between crops, so I will use no-tillage or minimal rotary tillage to save time and keep soil moisture. I will plant a hybrid variety — Denghai 605 has done well for me and my neighbors. For maize, I will apply about 16 kg of nitrogen, 4 kg of phosphorus, and 2 kg of potassium per mu, mostly as basal compound fertilizer with one topdressing at the big trumpet stage. Maize does not need as much water as wheat, but if the summer turns dry, I will irrigate twice, especially at silking and grain filling. I will spray pesticides twice — once for weeds and once for insects. I expect about 600 kg per mu for the maize.

My family needs both the grain and the income, so I will sell most of the maize and keep enough wheat for our own flour and some sale. This is my plan. I have done it many times before.
